title: The Natural History and Treatment of Acute Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) in HIV-positive Individuals
brief_summary: The aim of the study is to investigate the epidemiology, natural history and treatment outcomes of acute hepatitis C (HCV) infection. Given the current pattern of case reporting, the cohort will be largely made up of human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-positive patients, but HIV-negative patients with acute hepatitis C (AHC) will also be enrolled to enable comparisons to be made as appropriate and possible.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Documented current or past acute hepatitis C infection with detectable HCV-RNA (PCR-assay) with an estimated duration of 52 weeks at diagnosis as defined below:

  * First HCV RNA positive AND
  * Prior negative anti-HCV antibody or HCV RNA test within 12 months OR
  * Rise of liver transaminases above 2.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) within the past 12 months with prior normal transaminases during the year before AND
  * Exclusion of other causes of acute hepatitis

Exclusion Criteria:

* Acute liver disease other than hepatitis C
* Inability to provide written informed consent
* Younger than 18 years of age
study_population: 600 acute HCV infections with/without HIV infection
